channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Shocking death of former professor reverberates at Cambridge — and well beyond
item.dc:creator: Steve Hendrix
item.description: The death of Jason Arday, 41, came a little more than a week after he resigned from his post at the university amid accusations of plagiarism that ignited a culture-war firestorm.

item.title: At least 47 dead after 7.7-magnitude quake strikes Indonesia
item.dc:creator: Victoria Craw
item.description: The earthquake took place around 5 a.m. and was centered off the coast of Flores Island in the quake-prone archipelago.

item.title: How to beat an earthquake: The Colombian city where no one died
item.dc:creator: Helena Carpio
item.description: A deadly temblor devastated Armenia in 1999, spurring a reconstruction that allowed the city to build back stronger. When disaster struck this time, it was prepared.

item.title: Frustration with Trump grows among U.S.’s Persian Gulf allies, officials say
item.dc:creator: Susannah George
item.description: Gulf leaders worry the president is unable to manage the diplomacy necessary to secure peace with Iran, according to Arab and Western officials.

item.title: U.S., Canada race for deal to avert Trump’s threat of 50 percent tariffs
item.dc:creator: David J. Lynch
item.description: The tariffs are the latest exchange in a dispute that has disrupted the once harmonious — and nearly tariff-free — relationship over the past year.

item.title: A Nazi bunker stands in the way of Berlin’s housing plans
item.dc:creator: Maegan Vazquez
item.description: A plan to build apartments over the bunker is igniting debate on how Germany should address its complex history under Adolf Hitler.

item.title: IDF troops stood by as West Bank settlers besieged Palestinian homes
item.dc:creator: Gerry Shih, Heidi Levine
item.description: When Israeli extremists arrived in Qusra to force Palestinians from their homes, residents hoped the Israel Defense Forces would come to their aid.

item.title: FDA travels to Mexico a month after linking Taylor Farms to cyclospora outbreak
item.dc:creator: Rachel Roubein, Lena H. Sun, Caitlin Gilbert
item.description: Senior FDA official confirms that inspectors were on-site at the Taylor Farms processing facility and plan to be in the fields next.

item.title: Would Hong Wang have won her historic math prize if she had stayed in China?
item.dc:creator: Huiyee Chiew, Lyric Li, Rudy Lu
item.description: The success of Wang and other young Chinese mathematicians abroad has sparked discussion about the country’s education system.

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger released after 9 months, group says
item.dc:creator: Victoria Craw
item.description: Kevin Rideout was taken from outside his home in Niger’s capital in October, and U.S. officials scrambled to bring him home.

item.title: Poland says it thwarted Russian assassination attempt on U.S. citizen in Warsaw
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it was the first time Russia attempted to assassinate a U.S. citizen on the territory of another NATO member.

item.title: Farage beats Binface! But scandal still shadows Trump’s British ally.
item.dc:creator: Steve Hendrix
item.description: The election called by Reform UK’s leader was dismissed as a stunt by major parties, which declined to field candidates. A trash-can-wearing “alien” came in second with nearly 10,000 votes.
